data.name: Galactic Fighters
data.detailed_description:
• 5 Different Spaceships to Unlock and Drive

  • 15 Enhancements to customize the performance of your Spaceship

  • Third and First view

  • 5 Powerful end-level bosses to defeat

  • 13 long and difficult missions that require all your skill to be completed

  • 5 Different enemies whose only aim is to make you blow

  • An extra Boss Rush Mode. Only for true hardcore players (don't try this at home)

[quote=Unknown] In a distant future or in a remote past…

the Universe has been invaded by an interdimensional terrorist group called Bokor. Travelling through the spirals of Multiverso, Bokor has set up a base on our planet, with the intention of sucking all the vital energy out of it.

Most of the interplanetary races that have tried to defeat it have failed. On the contrary, others have formed an alliance with Bokor, with the illusion of being rewarded.

The operation “Riding a Wormhole” is the last chance of survival for our Universe: a suicide mission which consists in entering the solar system, where Bokor’s leader resides, and attacking him with an array of weapons specially designed to kill him.

chances Of Surviving Are Low.You are the captain of the “Human Spacial Navy” and you have volunteered for this crazy mission.

Captain! You are the last chance for all the races of this Universe! Are you ready to face the danger and risk your life for the safety of of your race and all the others? [/quote]

Galactic Fighters is a 3D space-shooter arcade bullet hell made up of 13 levels, in which the player has to fight against waves of enemy spaceships and bosses to prevent the galaxy from being destroyed by those creatures.

During your adventure you will be able to unlock and use several spaceships provided with weapons and unique characteristics.

What is more is that you could also buy many expansions for your spaceships, in order to improve them! Travel through different worlds, defeat waves of enemies and bosses... and save the galaxy! [spoiler]Or die trying! =D[/spoiler]

data.short_description: Galactic Fighters is a fast-paced single-player spaceship shooter arcade with roguelike elements, in 1st and 3rd person. Choose your spaceship, power it up, and get through hordes of aliens and bosses ready to destroy. Shoot, craft and loot your way to victory while the odds are stacked against you.

reviews.review:
Galactic Fighters is an ambitious independent space shooter that blends traditional arcade action with three-dimensional combat, bullet hell mechanics, and light roguelike progression. Developed by StarworkGC and published by StarworkGC alongside Fatum Games SL, the game delivers a straightforward experience centered on piloting armed spacecraft, eliminating hostile forces, and surviving increasingly dangerous encounters. Its appeal comes from the combination of challenging missions, customizable ships, and the freedom to switch between first-person and third-person perspectives. Although it lacks the refinement and complexity of larger productions, it offers an entertaining concept for players who appreciate old-school shooting challenges with a science-fiction setting.

The story revolves around an interdimensional terrorist organization called Bokor, which threatens the universe by draining a planet's vital energy. Numerous alien civilizations have attempted to resist this invasion, while others have chosen to cooperate with the enemy. Humanity responds with Operation Riding a Wormhole, a desperate military mission intended to eliminate the hostile leadership and prevent further destruction. Players assume the role of a Human Spacial Navy captain who volunteers for this dangerous assignment. The narrative establishes a reasonable justification for the battles, although storytelling is clearly secondary to gameplay. There is little emphasis on character development or elaborate world-building, making the experience more suitable for action enthusiasts than players seeking an emotionally engaging space adventure.

The gameplay focuses on navigating dangerous environments while destroying waves of enemy spacecraft. Across 13 challenging missions, players must demonstrate accurate shooting, quick reactions, and effective movement to survive. The bullet hell elements introduce additional pressure by forcing players to avoid incoming projectiles while maintaining offensive momentum. Unlike conventional two-dimensional shooters, the three-dimensional battlefield demands greater spatial awareness, making positioning and orientation particularly important. This approach provides an interesting variation on familiar arcade mechanics, although it can also make encounters more difficult to interpret when numerous projectiles and enemies appear simultaneously. The challenge should appeal to persistent players, but those expecting relaxed spaceship combat may find the experience unforgiving.

One of the more appealing mechanics is the ability to alternate between first-person and third-person perspectives. First-person gameplay creates a stronger sense of immersion, allowing players to experience battles directly from their spacecraft. Third-person viewing provides a wider understanding of the surrounding battlefield, which can be especially useful when avoiding enemy attacks. This flexibility encourages experimentation and allows players to approach combat according to their preferences. However, switching perspectives does not completely resolve the difficulties of navigating a three-dimensional shooting environment. Maintaining awareness of enemy positions and projectile trajectories can still become demanding, particularly during intense encounters.

Customization adds another layer of interest through five unlockable spacecraft and 15 available enhancements. Each ship offers its own characteristics and weapon capabilities, giving players reasons to experiment with different combat approaches. Upgrades provide opportunities to improve performance and prepare for increasingly difficult missions. The progression system introduces a welcome sense of accomplishment because players are not limited to relying entirely on their initial equipment. Nevertheless, the available customization options are relatively modest, and players expecting extensive equipment management or highly elaborate character-building mechanics may be disappointed. The system works best as a supplementary feature that strengthens the core arcade experience rather than as its primary attraction.

Enemy encounters provide much of the game's difficulty, although variety represents one of its noticeable limitations. There are five regular enemy types and five major bosses, meaning that players will inevitably become familiar with recurring threats. Boss battles offer particularly important challenges because they test movement, offensive efficiency, and the ability to recognize dangerous situations. The additional Boss Rush Mode expands the experience by concentrating on these demanding confrontations, providing an alternative for players who enjoy testing their combat mastery. However, the limited enemy roster can contribute to repetition throughout the campaign, especially when familiar encounters return without substantial mechanical changes.

The visual presentation embraces a modest three-dimensional science-fiction style, featuring spacecraft, alien threats, and environments designed around continuous combat. While the overall appearance supports the futuristic atmosphere, graphical sophistication is not among the game's strongest selling points. Its presentation is functional rather than spectacular, and the demanding nature of projectile-heavy encounters makes visual clarity particularly important. The audio and soundtrack help establish an arcade atmosphere, although the experience is ultimately driven more by gameplay mechanics than by audiovisual spectacle. Players who prioritize impressive graphics and cinematic presentation may find the production underwhelming, while those comfortable with simpler independent games may appreciate its direct approach.

Additional features include 19 Steam achievements, Steam Trading Cards, partial controller support, and a downloadable demo. These provide some extra incentive to explore the game and evaluate its mechanics before purchasing. The relatively modest system requirements are another advantage for players using less powerful computers. Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, the official Steam status is Unknown, meaning the game has not received a confirmed Verified or Playable classification. Although Linux support and partial controller compatibility are encouraging, they do not guarantee smooth handheld performance. Players should therefore consider Steam Deck functionality unverified and anticipate possible configuration adjustments.

Overall, Galactic Fighters is a respectable but limited arcade shooter that succeeds more through its challenging combat concept than through technical polish or extensive content. Its selectable camera perspectives, spacecraft upgrades, demanding missions, and Boss Rush Mode provide worthwhile entertainment for enthusiasts of traditional shoot 'em ups. However, repetitive enemy encounters, modest presentation, and relatively shallow progression prevent it from becoming a particularly memorable entry in the genre. It is best recommended to players who enjoy difficult space combat and appreciate smaller independent projects despite their limitations.

Rating: 6/10
